case.pattern_description: The transaction was a card-not-present online purchase made from a new device with proxy usage, and customer validation confirmed unauthorized use resulting in a confirmed fraud verdict in case CASE-HHG-010.
case.summary: Case HHG-010 resulted in a confirmed fraud verdict with $1,000.03 in financial exposure following a card-not-present transaction on a new device. Although the device fingerprint was shared by hundreds of other cards and indicated no organized ring, customer validation confirmed that the cardholder did not make the purchase and still possesses the physical card. Based on this customer denial and the high exposure, the card was blocked and a formal report was filed.

sar.narrative: This Suspicious Activity Report details case HHG-010 regarding customer C10434 and credit card C1043417379258.0150.0visa226.0credit, which incurred an unauthorized financial exposure of $1,000.03. On December 2, 2016, at 15:18:27, an online card-not-present transaction totaling $1,000.03 (Transaction ID 3506725) was executed using a newly introduced electronic device profile. A review of historical records indicates zero prior closed cases for this customer, while the device profile associated with the event has been linked to 417 distinct cards, suggesting a generalized operating system or browser fingerprint rather than a coordinated fraud ring. Upon bank notification, the customer promptly denied authorizing the purchase and confirmed physical possession of the card, validating that the transaction was fraudulent. In response to the confirmed unauthorized activity, the institution automatically generated an investigative case, immediately blocked the compromised card to prevent further losses, and initiated this regulatory filing due to the financial exposure exceeding the established reporting threshold.
